quiz.q: Which compile target is used to build Rust for the browser / generic WASM hosts?
options: wasm32-unknown-unknown
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
wasm32-wasi
browser-wasm32
quiz.explain: wasm32-unknown-unknown is the standard target for browser and generic WASM hosts — 32-bit WASM with no specific vendor or OS underneath it.

quiz.q: What does #[wasm_bindgen] on a function actually generate?
options: A unit test for the function
The marshalling/interop glue that lets JavaScript call the function and converts values between Rust and JS types
A benchmark harness
Documentation comments
quiz.explain: #[wasm_bindgen] generates the code that converts values (like String <-> JS string) across the boundary and emits a JS wrapper, so the function is directly callable from JavaScript.

quiz.q: What does `wasm-pack build` do that plain `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` does not?
options: Nothing extra — they're identical commands
It runs the wasm-bindgen CLI over the compiled output and assembles a ready-to-import pkg/ directory with JS glue and a package.json
It installs the wasm32-unknown-unknown target automatically
It publishes the crate to crates.io
quiz.explain: cargo build alone produces a raw .wasm file. wasm-pack build additionally runs wasm-bindgen's post-processing step and packages everything into an importable pkg/ directory.

quiz.q: Why can't Rust code compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown open a raw TCP socket?
options: It's a Rust language limitation unrelated to WASM
The browser sandbox doesn't expose raw sockets to WASM code at all — networking only happens through JS APIs like fetch or WebSocket
TCP sockets require a feature flag that's always disabled by default
It can, as long as std::net is imported
quiz.explain: The browser sandbox has no concept of raw sockets for WASM — any networking has to go through JavaScript-provided APIs like fetch() or WebSocket, which Rust code must call into.

quiz.q: What does console_error_panic_hook::set_once() do, and when should you call it?
options: It prevents panics from happening at all
It makes a panic's real message and location show up in the browser console instead of an opaque JS exception; call it once at startup during development
It disables all console output for performance
It converts panics into Result::Err automatically
quiz.explain: Without a panic hook, a Rust panic in WASM surfaces as an unhelpful, message-free JS runtime error. Installing the hook once at startup restores a real, readable panic message.

quiz.q: In Cargo.toml, what crate-type does wasm-bindgen's tooling need to produce a .wasm module plus JS bindings?
options: bin
cdylib
proc-macro
staticlib only, with no rlib
quiz.explain: wasm-bindgen's CLI post-processes a cdylib (C-compatible dynamic library) artifact. A plain rlib, the default library format, isn't something it can turn into a WASM+JS package.

quiz.q: What's the practical difference between `wasm-pack build --target web` and the default `--target bundler`?
options: There is no difference — both flags produce identical output
--target web generates an ES module you initialize yourself; --target bundler assumes a tool like webpack is handling that initialization step
--target web only works in Firefox
--target bundler skips generating a .wasm file entirely
quiz.explain: The generated JS glue differs by target. Using the wrong one breaks the import/init pattern your JS code expects, since web and bundler targets structure the output differently.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid making many small calls across the JS/Rust boundary with large or complex data?
options: wasm-bindgen has a hard limit of 10 calls per second
Each boundary crossing has real conversion/serialization cost, so many small calls with big payloads add up; typed arrays or serde-wasm-bindgen are better for bulk data
JavaScript can only call one Rust function per page load
It causes a compile error, not a performance issue
quiz.explain: Crossing the WASM/JS boundary isn't free — every call converts values between representations. For large data, prefer typed arrays or serde-wasm-bindgen over many small calls.

flashcards.front: Why is Rust an unusually good fit for compiling to WebAssembly?
flashcards.back: It has no garbage collector and a very small runtime, so compiled WASM stays small and fast without needing a language runtime shipped alongside it.

flashcards.front: What target do you compile Rust to for the browser, and how do you install it?
flashcards.back: wasm32-unknown-unknown, installed once per machine with `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
The interop glue that lets JavaScript call a Rust function directly — converting values like String <-> JS string automatically and emitting a matching JS/TypeScript wrapper.

flashcards.front: What does `wasm-pack build` do beyond a plain cargo build?
flashcards.back: It compiles to wasm32-unknown-unknown AND runs the wasm-bindgen CLI over the result, producing a pkg/ directory with the .wasm file, JS glue, types, and a package.json — ready to import or publish.

flashcards.front: Name three capabilities a browser-targeted WASM module does NOT have access to.
flashcards.back: A real filesystem (std::fs has nothing to act on), normal OS threads (std::thread::spawn doesn't work the usual way), and raw TCP/UDP sockets (only fetch/WebSocket via JS).

flashcards.front: What does an un-hooked panic look like in the browser console, and how do you fix it?
flashcards.back: An opaque, message-free error like 'RuntimeError: unreachable executed'. Call console_error_panic_hook::set_once() at startup (e.g. in a #[wasm_bindgen(start)] function) to get the real panic message and location.

flashcards.front: What crate-type must Cargo.toml declare for wasm-bindgen's tooling to work, and why?
flashcards.back: crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"] in [lib]. wasm-bindgen needs the cdylib (C-compatible dynamic library) artifact to post-process into a .wasm module plus JS bindings; rlib alone isn't enough.

flashcards.front: Why does crossing the JS/Rust boundary with large data need care?
flashcards.back: Each call across the boundary has real conversion cost. For big payloads, use typed arrays or serde-wasm-bindgen rather than many small individual calls.
